skill.name: biorxiv-database
skill.description: Search bioRxiv preprints by keyword, author, date, category, or DOI, retrieve structured metadata, and download selected PDFs.
skill.summary: Search bioRxiv metadata and download selected life sciences preprints.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The network requests and local file writes are confirmed, expected capabilities: the script contacts fixed bioRxiv HTTPS hosts and writes user-selected outputs. Hardcoded IP, certificate, reconnaissance, and shell-execution alerts are false positives caused by DOI examples, prose, keywords, and Markdown backticks. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: User-controlled output paths can overwrite existing local files.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths within an approved directory, reject existing files unless confirmed, and create downloads with exclusive write mode.

remediation.issue: PDF responses are buffered without content or size validation.
remediation.suggestion: Stream downloads with a size limit, require a PDF content type, and remove partial files after errors.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant bioRxiv preprints across dates and subjects can require repetitive API work. This skill searches metadata, filters results, and downloads selected PDFs.
actual_capabilities: Search preprints by keyword within user-specified dates.
Filter date-range searches by supported bioRxiv categories.
Find papers by author using case-insensitive metadata matching.
Retrieve detailed metadata for a supplied DOI.
Download a selected preprint PDF to a chosen local path.
Return standardized metadata to the terminal or a JSON file.
limitations: Requires internet access and the requests Python package.
Keyword and author matching occurs locally after date-range retrieval, which can be slow for broad searches.
PDF downloads always request version 1, even when newer versions exist.
It does not verify peer review status, study quality, citation accuracy, or publication outcomes.

use_cases.title: Review recent preprints
use_cases.description: Find focused bioRxiv results by topic, date range, and subject category.

use_cases.title: Track author activity
use_cases.description: Collect recent preprint metadata for a named researcher across a defined period.

use_cases.title: Build trend datasets
use_cases.description: Export structured metadata for downstream publication frequency and topic analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find recent preprints
prompt_templates.prompt: Find bioRxiv preprints about [topic] from [start date] to [end date]. Return key metadata and limit results to [number].

prompt_templates.title: Track an author
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for preprints by [author] between [start date] and [end date]. Save metadata to [filename] and summarize the matches.

prompt_templates.title: Review a category
prompt_templates.prompt: Search [bioRxiv category] for [keywords] during [date range]. Compare themes, methods, and publication dates across matching preprints.

prompt_templates.title: Build an evidence set
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a bioRxiv evidence set for [question]. Split [date range] into intervals, deduplicate DOIs, track versions, and identify screening candidates.

output_examples.input: Find CRISPR preprints in genomics from January through March 2025.
output_examples.output: A focused list of matching titles, authors, dates, DOIs, categories, abstracts, and bioRxiv links.

output_examples.input: Track preprints by a named researcher during the last year.
output_examples.output: An author-filtered result set with publication dates, metadata, and a concise match count.

output_examples.input: Retrieve one preprint by DOI and download its PDF.
output_examples.output: Detailed metadata for the DOI and the version 1 PDF saved at the requested path.

best_practices: Use narrow date ranges and category filters to reduce requests and local processing.
Review preprint versions and peer review status before treating results as established evidence.
Choose explicit output paths and verify available storage before downloading files.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad multi-year keyword searches without splitting the date range.
Do not treat substring matches as proof that a paper addresses the research question.
Do not overwrite important files with the output or PDF path options.

faq.question: Which source does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches public bioRxiv metadata through the official bioRxiv API and downloads PDFs from the bioRxiv website.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: No credentials are configured. The script uses public bioRxiv HTTPS endpoints.

faq.question: Which fields support keyword search?
faq.answer: Titles and abstracts are searched by default. Author metadata can be included through the search-fields option.

faq.question: Can it download full papers?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a DOI and an explicit local path for the PDF.

faq.question: Does PDF download select the latest version?
faq.answer: No. The current download method always requests version 1, so verify newer versions separately.

faq.question: Does it search medRxiv?
faq.answer: No. The implementation is limited to bioRxiv life sciences preprints.
